meeting_header:
Date: 2028-07-30
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Aaron Cho (Redwood SE), Daniel Lee (Nimbus VP Eng), Priya Reddy (Nimbus SRE), Tom Nguyen (Nimbus Security)
summary: High-level walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Focus on how to triage failures, correlate traces to request-ids, and export logs for debugging. Discussed Nimbus's concerns about latency/cost, VPC/private deployment, and SOC2/compliance. Agreed next steps: share security docs, run a small benchmark against staging traces, and provide a trial account.
topics: Correlating traces to requests and KV cache hits
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, I'm Sofia from Redwood. Hey Aaron is on as well, he'll run the console walkthrough.
[00:06] Daniel: Hi, Daniel here, thanks for setting this up.
[00:08] Priya: Priya from infra, quick heads up we'll focus mostly on debugging and logs.
[00:12] Aaron: Cool, great. Quick agenda — tracing UI, error analysis, request logs, and then some debugging flows. We'll show how to correlate request-id to traces.
[00:20] Tom: Security person on line, Tom — will want to see audit logs, KMS integration, netw- network details.
[00:25] Sofia: Perfect. Daniel can you give 60 seconds on current stack and pain points?
[00:30] Daniel: Sure. We run services in k8s on GCP; currently sending inference requests to OpenAI hosted and a small self-hosted Llama cluster. We're seeing occasional 5xx spikes, slow tails around 800-1k ms, and debugging is hard — logs are scattered and we can't tie an OpenAI response to a user action. Also worried about PII in logs and SOC2.
[00:51] Aaron: Ok, that's common. We'll show tracing + request logs and how Redwood ties tokens, model variants, and backend fallbacks into the trace.
[01:02] Sofia: Quick qualification — do you plan to use Hosted Redwood API initially or go Dedicated/private?
[01:08] Daniel: We'd prefer hosted to move fast but need private for PCI scope later. So hybrid is likely.
[01:15] Priya: Also curious about trace retention and export for long term SLO analysis.
[01:20] Aaron: Great. Jumping into the console — I'm sharing screen — apologies if the auto caption is off.
[01:28] Aaron: On the tracing tab you can see a list of recent traces; each trace has overall latency, token counts, model used, and a request-id that maps to a request-log.
[01:37] [screen noise]
[01:40] Aaron: Here's an example trace labeled with a 502 error during model decode — you can expand spans to see model call, batching layer, and K-V cache hit/miss. Note: occasionally the transcript will show K-V cash instead of KV cache — common ASR mis-typo.
[01:55] Priya: Can you filter traces by model and region? We run in us-central and europe-west.
[02:00] Aaron: Yep, you can filter by model tag, region, and deployment (hosted vs dedicated). Also by error type — 4xx, 5xx, timeout.
[02:08] Daniel: How do we correlate a user-facing uuid to this trace?
[02:12] Aaron: Good question — we support passing a customer_request_id header. That shows up in the trace metadata; you can search request-logs by that id and jump to the exact trace.
[02:21] Daniel: Nice.
[02:22] Aaron: Also we surface prefix cache hit ratio — if a request hits the KV cache the trace will show a cache span with hit:true, which helps diagnose slow tails from cold cache.
[02:32] Priya: Do you capture model variant fallbacks? E.g., fallback to cheaper quantized model?
[02:36] Aaron: Yes, fallbacks are recorded as spans. We show the routing decision, which variant ran, and token counts — helpful for cost/regression analysis.
[02:44] Tom: On the security side, where are these traces stored and how long?
[02:49] Sofia: For hosted customers you can configure retention; for Private we install a customer-controlled control plane — data residency is configurable and logs can route to your own S3 or GCS bucket. We support KMS for envelope encryption.
[02:59] Tom: Is audit logging separate? Need admin-level change records.
[03:03] Aaron: Audit logs are separate and include API key usage, role changes, and console actions. We can stream them to your syslog or SIEM.
[03:10] Daniel: Can you show an error-analysis view?
[03:13] Aaron: Yup. Switching to error analysis — this aggregates by error fingerprint, shows sample stack traces, frequency over time, and top-affected routes. You can click a fingerprint to see representative request-logs and traces.
[03:26] [short pause while UI loads]
[03:30] Aaron: Here's an example of repeated 502s tied to an internal model OOM on a dedicated pool we were simulating. You can group by route or user-id.
[03:40] Priya: The grouping looks handy — can we export aggregated metrics to Datadog?
[03:44] Aaron: Yes, we have integrations to push aggregates and traces to Datadog, NewRelic, and can also push raw request-logs to your storage.
[03:51] Daniel: What does a request-log entry look like?
[03:54] Aaron: It contains timestamp, request-id, customer_request_id if provided, route/model, token counts, latency breakdown (queue, model, tokenization), and raw model response payload (optionally redacted).
[04:07] Priya: About redaction — we need PII redaction before sending logs.
[04:11] Sofia: We have configurable scrubbing rules and can apply server-side redaction patterns, or for private deployments you can keep logs in your network and run your own redaction pipeline.
[04:21] Tom: How about encryption at rest?
[04:24] Aaron: SSL in transit, envelope encryption at rest and you can plug your own KMS or HSM for key management.
[04:30] Daniel: Walk me through a debugging flow — from an alert to root cause.
[04:33] Aaron: Sure. Step 1: Alert (we integrate with PagerDuty) -> click alert to open error analysis -> find fingerprint -> sample request-log -> open trace -> expand spans to see which stage (routing, batching, model) caused the latency or error -> if needed, export the raw request payload to reproduce against a sandbox.
[04:52] Daniel: Can you show a live example? We had a spike yesterday around 14:12 — I can paste a request-id.
[04:58] Priya: I'll paste a sanitized id now.
[05:01] Daniel: request-id: nimbus-20280729-14-12-7c9f
[05:07] Aaron: Searching... found it. Here's the trace. I see a long model latency span and a small retry loop. There's also a cache miss on KV span.
[05:18] Aaron: The model decode span shows OOM-ish memory pressure logs; there's a note that the model switched to a fallback smaller quantized variant during that request.
[05:28] Priya: That explains the increased tokenization time we saw.
[05:31] Aaron: Right — you can click 'Export trace' which packages the request-log and trace and optionally a repro payload.
[05:36] Daniel: Can we mark sensitive fields before export?
[05:39] Aaron: Yes you can mask fields in the request-log view and set default export redaction rules.
[05:44] Tom: On-prem / VPC question — if we run Private, do traces still show model internals? We can't have model artifacts leave our network.
[05:52] Sofia: With Private deployment the control plane can be customer-hosted; only metadata pointers leave if you want. We can also provide a fully air-gapped option for regulated customers.
[06:02] Priya: Nice. Latency numbers in the trace — are they broken down per-token or aggregated?
[06:06] Aaron: Per-span timings include per-token averages for model decode spans, and you can zoom into token-by-token timing in the timeline.
[06:13] Daniel: How accurate are tokenization estimates across models?
[06:16] Aaron: We use tokenizer libs matched to each model; but sometimes transcripts may show 'token-nizer' spelled weirdly, that's just internal UI copy errors we've been cleaning up.
[06:25] [laughter]
[06:28] Aaron: Switching to request logs tab — here's a live query of yesterday's traffic. You can filter by route, status, model, or custom metadata.
[06:35] Priya: Can queries be saved and scheduled?
[06:37] Aaron: Yes, saved queries and alerts; also ability to export CSV or stream to your storage.
[06:42] Daniel: We want a dashboard showing 5xx rate over time with breakdown by model variant.
[06:47] Aaron: You can create a chart in the console and pin to a dashboard; charts can aggregate by route or model.
[06:52] Priya: For long term SLOs, what's retention policy?
[06:55] Sofia: Hosted default 90 days for traces, longer retention as paid add-on; for Dedicated and Private you control retention.
[07:03] Tom: About compliance: can we get a SOC2 package and pen-test report?
[07:06] Sofia: Yes, we'll send the SOC2 summary and compliance docs in the next steps.
[07:10] Daniel: Is there integration for SSO? We use Okta.
[07:13] Aaron: SSO/SAML is supported, RBAC with roles, and we've got SCIM for provisioning.
[07:19] Priya: Ok. A few technical nitty-grittys — how heavy is the client instrumentation? We don't want to change request latency by much.
[07:25] Aaron: Instrumentation is a lightweight header and optional SDK; most of the work is server-side. For latency-sensitive paths you can enable async logging.
[07:33] Daniel: If we use Redwood SDK, will batching be automatic? We have bursts and want to tune batch sizes.
[07:38] Aaron: Yes batching is automatic in the runtime, but you can configure batching policies per route and override in Dedicated. Redwood Optimize can recommend batch sizes based on your workload.
[07:48] Priya: That Optimize feature — can it propose quantization profiles too?
[07:51] Aaron: It gives model and quantization recommendations tied to cost/quality tradeoffs and suggests configs.
[07:58] Daniel: What's the typical time to onboard a staging environment?
[08:01] Sofia: For hosted it's minutes; for dedicated it's usually a few days for capacity and routing; private can be weeks depending on networking.
[08:10] Daniel: Ok. Any rate limit visibility in the console?
[08:13] Aaron: There's a throttling view that shows per-key and per-route rate-limit hits and token consumption.
[08:18] Priya: We need per-tenant quotas.
[08:20] Aaron: Multi-tenant quotas are supported and you can set per-tenant rate limits and cost centers.
[08:26] [brief pause]
[08:30] Daniel: About the repro flow — if we export a repro payload can we replay it to a sandbox of our model?
[08:36] Aaron: Yes, export creates a tar with input, model version, and headers; you can replay against a sandbox endpoint or our sandbox runner.
[08:43] Tom: How do you handle secrets in the payload?
[08:46] Aaron: We redact by default if patterns match and allow customer-specified redaction rules.
[08:52] Priya: For benchmarking, what's the best way to measure p95/p99 tail?
[08:56] Aaron: Use request logs to compute latency percentiles and attach traces for p99 samples. We can run an automated benchmark with your staging traffic to produce a report.
[09:05] Daniel: That would be helpful.
[09:07] Aaron: I'll note that as an action.
[09:10] Sofia: Quick question — cost visibility at token level?
[09:13] Aaron: Console shows token-level cost breakdown per-route and per-model; you can also see cost impact of caching and batching.
[09:20] Daniel: Are there alert templates for sudden cost spikes?
[09:23] Aaron: Yep, set alerts on spend rate or token burn per minute.
[09:27] [background noise]
[09:30] Daniel: Let's talk about a concrete pilot — we want Redwood to run for our chat support routing route for 2 weeks. What would you need?
[09:38] Sofia: For a pilot we'll provide a trial account, test keys, setup a staging project, and run a benchmark against a subset of traffic. We'll need a point-of-contact on your side — looks like Priya.
[09:46] Priya: Yep, that's me.
[09:48] Sofia: Great. Next steps recap: Sofia will send pricing + SOC2 docs; Aaron will run a sample benchmark and share traces; Priya will provide sanitized logs and staging keys.
[09:59] Daniel: Timeline for pilot? We can start next week if we get keys.
[10:03] Sofia: We'll aim to set up staging by 2028-08-02 and kick off benchmark the week of 8/4.
[10:10] Tom: One last question — do you support custom plugins or tool-calling tracing? We have some toolchain integrations.
[10:16] Aaron: We capture tool calls as spans and you can plug in structured outputs. Tool-calling traces show tool inputs/outputs with optional masking.
[10:25] Priya: Good to know.
[10:26] Sofia: Any other questions?
[10:29] Daniel: Not right now, thanks for the thorough walkthrough.
[10:31] Aaron: Cool. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[10:33] Priya: Thanks all.
[10:35] Sofia: Thanks, meeting adjourned. Recap in follow-up email with recording and next steps.
[10:40] [call ends]
